_doc: src: glb filename under models-src/. texSrc: optional hand-edited PNG (Krita) replacing the glb's embedded base-color texture; defaults to <label>.png if present. emissiveSrc: optional hand-painted emissive PNG (black except glowing parts, same UVs as base) — added as the emissive map, scaled by emissiveStrength (HDR>1 so bloom catches it); emissiveStrength 0 means GLOW OFF and skips the map entirely, so the glb carries no dead texture — re-enabling a prop's glow is one number. roughness: optional roughnessFactor, which glTF MULTIPLIES by the MR map's green channel, so the map's own variation survives and only its level moves — the specular dial, since a TRELLIS bake lands uniformly matte (green p05..p95 ~0.71-0.94) and catches no highlight. Do not take it far below 0.3 or to 0: GGX specular is a2/(PI*d^2) with a2 = roughness^4, and against the tunnel's 45-candela spotlights a near-mirror surface peaks past the half-float post buffer's 65504 = Infinity, which UnrealBloom smears into a black frame (docs/3d-changes.md). tris: meshopt-simplify target tri count (<= source); -1 keeps full geometry (no decimate). error: meshopt distortion cap (smaller=more detail). tex: baked-texture max edge px. dropMR: true strips the metallic-roughness map (matte 0/1) — temp kill of metal/gloss. baseColor: [r,g,b,a] LINEAR baseColorFactor multiplied onto the base map — darkens a prop whose authored albedo is far brighter than the game art. lift: gamma on the base-colour MAP itself, out = (v/255)**lift, so <1 BRIGHTENS — the inverse of baseColor, which is a factor in [0,1] and can only go down. For a prop the generator bakes too dark: a subject dense enough to occlude itself has that occlusion baked into its albedo (wild/bush-bramble, 0.44x where a conifer is 0.79x), and repainting the reference cannot fix it without out-brightening the flat backdrop TRELLIS segments against. Same knob name and meaning as textures.json's lift. tex is not free to lower: divide it by the tri count to get TEXELS PER TRIANGLE and keep it near what the source was authored at (a TRELLIS 2048 export is ~43), or the map is not shrunk but deleted. seed/seed100k: the TRELLIS seeds this glb and its -100k master were generated with, so either can be reproduced from the archived <label>-src.png with image_to_3d at the same decimation_target — but STATE THE SETTINGS EXPLICITLY for anything generated before 2026-08-23: the MCP default moved remesh_project 0.8 -> 0.9 and now also sends meshCluster {1,0,1,PI/2}, so those props do NOT reproduce on today's defaults. TRELLIS is not bit-deterministic anyway, so a seed reproduces the look, not the file. provenance only — make models never reads them. last_converted/last_sig: mtime+param cache written by make models — editing any input or param rebuilds automatically.

facility/lamp-post.note: the facility compound's own lamp: a modern slim tapered mast with a shrouded downlight head cantilevered on a short arm, instanced along the walkway kerb and through the park (render.facility.FacilityLamps). the `src` IS the 100k master - there is no second generation run, because models.mjs decimates out of it into app/models and never writes back over it, so the archive and the source are one file. 1.22x split, so the offline route works. COMPONENTS READ 3 AT 70.4% AND THE GATE CALLS THAT A REJECT - it is not one, for exactly the reason wild/guard-rail records: the three pieces are the MAST (34,840 verts), the HEAD (12,211) and the BASE PLATE (2,439), which is what the object is made of, and that is the shipped conifer's 2-at-51/49 shape rather than the 96-at-24% blob cloud the gate exists to catch. its reference came back IN BAND on the first try (subject luma p50 71 against the 69-77 that bakes correctly) and needed no in-code correction - and propstat's own --lift must NOT be used on it: charcoal steel against the #5a5d63 backdrop leaves a subject margin of only 14, so lift's soft key lands at alpha 0.54 and would composite the mast half-dissolved into its own backdrop. baked at atlas mean 139/140/141, far over the 46-52 family, so baseColor is a straight linear darken. MR came back metal max 219 - dropMR, or it renders BLACK under debug key 1 rather than chrome. THE EMISSIVE MAP IS GENERATED, NOT PAINTED, and that is the answer to "the atlas layout is unknown" that an earlier pass gave up on: it is built by tools/emissive.py off the BUILT glb (never the master, or the mask misses a chart the decimation moved), regenerate with: python3 tools/emissive.py app/models/facility/lamp-post.glb -o models-src/facility-lamp-post-emissive.png --box=-0.05,0.05,0.445,0.4845,0.036,0.13 --res 320 --dilate 1 --tint 9db4d4 --preview /tmp/prev.png. that box is the head's LENS AND SIDES WITH THE TOP EXCLUDED (the top face is the band y > 0.4859): 194 tris, 7.0% of the surface, 4.4% of the atlas. three earlier boxes are worth not repeating. the WHOLE head box read as a glowing white card, because the head is a flat slab whose biggest face is the top and the camera looks down. filtering that by averaged NORMAL (ny < -0.5) fixed nothing, because the strays it was blamed for were the DILATION crossing into neighbouring charts - 22 unselected triangles lit from y -0.498 to +0.484, i.e. the mast down to the base plate. and the LENS ALONE (y up to 0.456) is physically right and invisible: the head is 0.35 x 0.20 x 0.43 world units and its underside faces away from an overhead camera, so nothing on the fixture glowed and only the cone and the ground pool said it was on. author at tex (320), not 512, or models.mjs's resize puts back the ramp the bleed mask removed. it replaced an additive quad hung at the bulb, which was fixed-yaw (the render.particles.Sprites FRONTAL pose) on a mast that yaws to face the surface it lights, so the card sat across the housing at an arbitrary angle and read as a sticker. tris 1500 is 'as low as it will go' — the seam network floors it at 2,434 — and tex is sized for THAT count and not for a power of two: 256 put it at 26 texels/tri, well under the ~43-55 a TRELLIS 2048 export is authored at, which does not shrink the map but deletes it. 320 lands on 42

ITS FRONT MOVED. the old model lay along local z and faced +z; this one lies along local Z with its DEPTH on x, and the backrest measures at mean x -0.138 against the mesh's own -0.012, so the bench faces local +X and render.facility.FacilityGround.facing carries a -PI/2 for it. bbox widest/height 1.52, not the old 1.98, so FacilityStyle.PARK_BENCH_H had to move too - it is sized for the LENGTH, which is what reads from overhead. reference took propstat's --lift 73 (subject p50 58 against the 69-77 that bakes correctly). baked at atlas mean 58/66/59, GREEN rather than neutral, so baseColor is a per-channel correction and not a flat darken. THEN ASKED TO COME DOWN 20% IN BRIGHTNESS, 0.95 -> 0.76, and baseColor is a LINEAR factor so that is 20% of LIGHT and about 16% of what the screen shows: MEASURED over the rack's own 97,897 pixels on one frame, rendered luma 23.1 -> 19.5, a ratio of 0.842. A TRUE 20% OFF THE DISPLAYED VALUE WOULD BE baseColor ~0.58 AND IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE - the floor in front of this rack renders at luma 18.4, so 0.76 already leaves it only +1.1 over its own background (0.95 was +4.8) and 0.58 puts it under, which is exactly the hole the 0.65 fit above was rejected for. sRGB IS NOT LINEAR AND THE KNOB IS: when a brightness cut is asked for in percent, say which space it landed in. The knob is the new `sat` in tools/models.mjs, the same Rec.709-in-linear-light mix textures.json's own `sat` and the `spriteSat` uniform are, so 0.5 means one thing everywhere. PER-PIXEL LUMINANCE IS UNTOUCHED BY CONSTRUCTION and the atlas channel MEAN still moves, 135/91/27 -> 121/97/81: that statistic is an sRGB-byte average and the transfer curve is concave, so three channels converging on one luminance average higher. MR came back metal mean 132 - dropMR, which strips a map the Lambert path never samples anyway. THE VALUE WAS RAISED FROM 49 TO 78 (baseColor 0.21 -> 0.60), which is the same call facility/gas-cylinders records and applies to every prop that stands INDOORS: the 46-52 family was fitted outdoors against asphalt, and after the interior repaint the room floor's albedo is 95 and the wall's 111, so a prop at 49 renders as a hole. measured before the raise, on one frame, this trolley's shelf top rendered at luma 13.9 - level with the generator's own bench tops at 16.1 and a sixth of the floor's 86. it stays NEUTRAL, and that is correct rather than an oversight: a trolley is bare steel, so the flat 0.60 moves only the level and the bake's own cool 91/100/108 lean survives into 72/79/86 RE-FITTED 0.60 -> 0.85 once the indoor fill stopped being flat (IndoorMaskOpts.bounce). The 0.60 was measured against a normal-blind ambient that rendered every face of this prop as one value, and a baseColor FACTOR is linear - it scales the albedo's own frame-vs-shelf SEPARATION by exactly as much as it scales the level. Measured on one frame over the prop's own 2,476 pixels: 0.60 gives sd 12.00 at prop-minus-background +11.8, 0.75 gives 12.97 at +19.0, 0.85 gives 13.64 at +22.6, 1.0 gives 15.31 at +36.2. THE ALBEDO IS WHAT CARRIES THE METAL READ and this is the knob that buys it: the reference is bright tube frames against dark shelf slabs and near-black castors with almost no highlight anywhere in it, and the MR map cannot help - measured, its metallic channel is mean 132 sd 22.9 with p05..p95 of 105..149, i.e. UNIFORM half-metal carrying no frame-vs-shelf information at all, which is what dropMR above was right to throw away. AND THE ALBEDO HAS NO FRAME-VS-SHELF SEPARATION EITHER, which corrects the paragraph above: the luma histogram of the baked 2048 atlas puts 88.19% of its texels in a SINGLE 16-count band (96-111), with 9.46% in 80-95 and ~2% of unwrapped gutter below 48. The reference's bright tubes against dark slabs is not in the bake at all, so baseColor moves the LEVEL and nothing else, and the sd it was fitted against was shading, AO and the indoor fill rather than albedo. A `roughness` KEY WAS TRIED HERE AND REVERTED: 0.4 holds the prop on MeshStandard (render.Models.toLambert returns unchanged below 1) and gives it a real GGX specular, and it is worth exactly nothing indoors - measured over the prop's own 23.6k pixels, roughness 1.0/0.4/0.2 read mean 66.41/66.25/65.98 with p99 and max BIT-IDENTICAL, because every analytic light in the room is only 3.3% of this prop's pixel. The glint lives in render.world.PropEnv's `sheen` lobe instead; do not re-add the key.

facility/deco-rack.note: THE FIRST OF THE FACILITY'S FITTINGS TO TAKE THE BLENDER ROUTE, and it runs BESIDE the four quads render.facility.FacilityDeco still emits -- FacilityStyle.DECO_RACK_GLB switches between them and nothing is deleted, so the A/B is one flag. What the quads cannot state is that a rack is not a slab: it is SIX CHASSIS in a frame, each set back behind its own bezel, on a skirted foot under an overhanging lid. Six is not a style choice, it is DECO_RACK_H / (DECO_RACK_TILE / 3) -- the art holds three chassis per tile and getting the count wrong put half a chassis at the lid once already (DECO_RACK_H's own note). 1,404 tris against the quads' 8, measured on the evaluated mesh at 1.660 x 3.200 x 1.2385, z_min 0; facility/deco-rack-low is its one-tile sibling out of the same script. SECOND PASS PUT AN EDGE BREAK ON EVERY ARRIS (buildlib.chamfer, EDGE 0.014, two segments, the new strips smooth-shaded and the flats left flat) -- reported as the fittings wanting some edge smoothing, and it is what turns a mathematical corner into a lit line at this camera. It is GEOMETRY and not a bevel modifier: the modifier interpolates each new strip's UVs between the faces it joins, so a strip between a face on cell 0 and one on cell 1 sweeps diagonally across the whole packed sheet; the strips here are made before the unwrap and tagged with a plain swatch. Smoothing only the strips is also deliberate -- shade the flats too and every large face picks up a corner gradient, because a bevel's corner normal tilts by the same angle however narrow it is. A CUBE HAS SIX FACES AND AN EMITTED FITTING HAS FOUR -- FacilityDeco.unit puts out a front, two flanks and a lid and no bottom at all, so an assembly of boxes brings back faces the quads never had and the first build had three exactly coplanar pairs (carcass bottom against the skirt's AND against the floor plane, carcass top against the lid's, three backs in the masonry), reported as z-fighting top and bottom. DELETING THEM WAS THE WRONG FIX AND LEFT THE MESH FULL OF HOLES, reported next: a prop is a solid, and a face the camera never meets still bounds it. Every box is CLOSED and the planes are pulled apart instead -- CARC_IN 0.02 off the carcass head so the lid's top owns that plane, TRIM_IN 0.05 pulling the skirt and the lid INSIDE the carcass front and back (flush fights the carcass's own face, proud lands a hair in front of the chassis bezel over it, and 0.05 is what clears the top chassis's lid sitting 0.009 under the cap's). Floors are exempt and stack on z = 0, because nothing sees under a fitting. buildlib.check reports holes and near-coplanar co-facing pairs on every object before export and both cabinets read 0 and 0. THE SKIRT AND THE LIP TAKE NO HEIGHT AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: FacilityDeco.lights puts a rack's status specks at h * (r + 0.5) / rows off the same chassis count, so spending height on a base and a lid would have moved every chassis up to a sixth of its own height away from its own lights. They stand PROUD instead and the total is exactly DECO_RACK_H. NO NEW ART: tools/modelsheet.py packs the BUILT labels (facility/deco-rack, -side, -top) into models-src/facility/rack-sheet.png, so each one's own fitted lift is already in the pixels and this entry carries no baseColor, no lift and no sat. A chassis front takes a THIRD of the front cell -- the image holds three and a sub-rect of a sheet may not wrap. THE SAME FACT IS WHY EACH CELL IS PRE-TILED: localFace divides a face by DECO_RACK_TILE on both axes, so a flank carries 0.75 across its depth by 2.0 up its height, and a cell mapped 0..1 over the whole face stretched that square art 2.67x -- reported from the game as stretched sides. Walking u past a cell edge is not available, so modelsheet.py's --repeat bakes the repeat into the cell instead (flank 0.75x2.0, lid 1.05x0.75, and cell 3 the same flank at 0.75x1.0 for the low cabinet). propstat REJECTs it at 9 components / 12.5% largest and calls it UNDECIMATABLE at 3.25x split: nine components is nine boxes (carcass, skirt, lip, six chassis) and both lines are TRELLIS gates reading a hand-made assembly. tex 512 puts the front face at 113 texels per world unit against the ground's 57; 256 would put it at 56, level with the floor it stands on. PASS 7: baked AO. `ao` is FITTED so the bake costs 20% of the prop's LEVEL and no more (mean COLOR_0 = 0.80, one step from `ao * 0.20 / (1 - mean)`), because every prop here was value-fitted and a flat 0.55 drops some of them 37%. Shipped ao 0.55, aoReach 0.45.

facility/deco-cabinet.note: the storage cabinet, second fitting down the Blender route (models-src/facility/cabinet_build.py) and the first one whose case is ONLY the draw call. facility/deco-shelving.note: BASECOLOR 0.80 SINCE, PASS 8, reported from the game as the new decoration looking bright. No repaint: the pixels are shared and every fitted value in them is somebody else's. the open storage shelving standing against a laboratory or office wall (models-src/facility/store_build.py, render.facility.FacilityDeco.fittings behind FacilityStyle.DECO_SHELF_GLB). 204 tris, 2.600 x 1.666 x 2.600, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair. Here the frame is members: four uprights, four cross rails and a brace to each end, three perforated plates, and the daylight through the middle of it is real. NO NEW ART AND NOT ONE PIXEL OF IT: tools/modelsheet.py packs the BUILT facility/deco-shelf-side and facility/deco-shelf-top into models-src/facility/store-sheet.png, shared with facility/lab-trolley-hand, so the unit standing in a lab is the same steel as the unit that stood there before it and every fitted lift is already in the pixels -- no baseColor, no lift, no sat. CELL 0 IS TILED 1.561x IN U, which is the finding worth keeping: modelsheet stretches a non-square source into its square cell and deco-shelf-side is 328 x 512, so a straight pack would have put OVAL slots on the uprights; tiled 1.561 the first copy lands 1:1 at u 0..0.6406 and ONE CELL TEXEL IS 0.005078 WORLD UNITS on both axes, which is what lets every rect be read straight off the pixels. THE GEOMETRY IS READ OFF THE ART: the uprights are columns 4..31 (0.142 wide) and the four rails rows 11-35 / 142-166 / 304-328 / 467-492, whose CENTRES land on 0.955, 0.699, 0.383 and 0.0635 of the height -- FacilityStyle.DECO_SHELF_Y plus DECO_SHELF_TOP_Y to three decimals. THE BRACE IS LIGHTER STOCK THAN A RAIL (0.05 against 0.09) and that is not decoration: at the same width its two flanks landed on the rails' own planes and buildlib.check called eight z-fights. Cells 1 and 2 are the SAME plate at two pre-tiled periods, 4.22x2.51 here and 3.60x1.64 on the trolley, because a hand-modelled face maps its cell 0..1 and cannot wrap -- one period could not serve two shelf sizes at DECO_SHELF_TILE 0.55. AND THE BOXES ARE GONE FROM THE MODEL: FacilityDeco.boxes used to stand 1..3 crates on every plate of every unit and nothing else ever, so a unit was the same object every time; the three plates are clutter LIDS now (FacilityClutter.lid) and a crate is one of the things dealt into them. PASS 6, four reports at once: the plate is 0.03 and not 0.06 (reported too thick -- and FacilityStyle.DECO_SHELF_PLATE_Y is DERIVED from it, 0.0398 -> 0.0283, or every clutter box on the unit floats), its UNDERSIDE takes the same perforated cell on the same window because a punched plate is punched from below, and the two LONG sides finally carry members -- a tie at each of the four levels plus one diagonal, in lighter section. THE TIES STOP INSIDE THE UPRIGHTS: run to the full width they cross the end rails at the four corners with both lids on ONE plane, sixteen z-fights, and ending on the post's inner face buried 0.02 past it leaves no coincident plane anywhere. Their 0.09 thickness is also load-bearing -- it is what keeps the diagonal's flanks the 0.02 clear of theirs that BRACE_D was fitted for. The long-side braces forced brace() out as a function and found a place() trap worth knowing: bl.place PITCHES ABOUT X BEFORE IT TRANSLATES, so a bar already standing off-centre in y swings instead of tilting. 204 -> 324 tris, dims unchanged, holes 0 / coplanar 0 / 0 smears. PASS 7. `ao` 0.29 at aoReach 0.45 — the shelf gap is 0.827 over a span of 2.6, so a shorter reach cannot see the shelf above. Strength is low because an open frame sees itself everywhere: at a flat 0.55 the mean COLOR_0 was 0.625, i.e. the unit lost 37% of its level. Shelves also carry a centre vertex and a broken arris. 324 -> 528 tris. PASS 9, two reports off one polygon probe and both were the two diagonals. THE FRONT DIAGONAL IS GONE: both long sides carried one and a bay is loaded through its front, so a real one braces the back panel and the two end frames and never the opening. +y is the BACK and that is derived rather than guessed -- FacilityDeco yaws a fitting to face AWAY from its masonry, so glTF +z at yaw 0 is blender -y. The front keeps its four horizontal ties, which is what a shelving bay actually has. AND 'THESE LOOK UNTEXTURED' WAS CORRECT: every brace face wore R_STEEL, a deliberate 1x1-TEXEL rect, on the argument that a stated window projects to a LINE on a turned piece's end faces. That is true of buildlib.tag, which defers the projection to unwrap and so measures the bbox AFTER the turn, and false of flat_uv, which states the axes per face BEFORE it and marks the face -1 so unwrap skips it -- so the braces go through member() now and wear the RAIL strip down their flanks with the plain swatch on their ends. propstat reports 0 uv smears either way, so the flat colour was buying nothing. 528 -> 516 tris, dims unchanged at 2.600 x 1.666 x 2.600, holes 0 / coplanar 0. PASS 10, a probe pick on the TOP PLATE'S FRONT EDGE reported as 'u,v on a very small tex part': every plate edge wore R_PLAIN, 14 x 12 texels over a 2.6 x 0.03 face, a 37x smear. They take R_EDGE now, a 6-row slice down the middle of rail 2 (rows 151..157, cols 40..290) -- 6 rows IS 0.03 at 0.005078 units per texel, and the 2x stretch runs along the brushed grain. 516 tris unchanged, holes 0 / coplanar 0 / smears 0.

AND THE TRAY CAME OFF THE PERFORATED CELL: it had the shelving's holes only because the sheet had them. store-sheet cell 2 is now facility/table-top, the lab bench's OWN worktop, so the trolley wears the same surface as the benches beside it -- taken as a SUB-RECT (0.396 x 0.18 of one repeat) and not a baked --repeat, because at BENCH_TOP_TILE 5.0 a 1.98 x 0.902 tray wants less than one repeat and modelsheet cannot express that. One check finding: at WHEEL_W 0.07 the wheel's discs sat 0.0075 off the stem's flanks, eight near-coplanar pairs, so the wheel is 0.09 wide. 268 -> 740 tris against the TRELLIS bake's 5,915; dims 1.98 x 0.902 x 2.0 unchanged, so KIT_TROLLEY_W/D hold. AO BAKED (0.55, aoRes 128) to match the TRELLIS lab-trolley this replaced, which shipped with it: an open frame is the case AO was added for - no light in the game reaches the inside of one, and the term is the only thing that darkens the underside of a tray or the well between two legs. PASS 7. Tray UV was 51 texels/world against the shelving plate's 110 — a cell is HALF the sheet and tex 512 downsizes the 1024 atlas again, so `bl.sub`ing a 1x1 cell threw three quarters of the texels away. Cell 2 now carries the 0.396x0.1804 crop itself and the tray takes the whole cell: 251 shipped texels, 51 -> 80/world, the source's own ceiling. aoReach 0.6 because the TRAY GAP is 0.75 against a span of 2.0 — the default 0.35 reach is 0.70 and never saw the shelf above. Lower tray lid COLOR_0 0.908 -> 0.829 against the upper's 0.959 (it was 0.931 on BOTH). Legs wear a painted highlight, luma 49..98 round the turn against the grip's flat 96..98; treads wear a perforation hole at 47.4. 740 -> 1044 tris. facility/janitor-broom.note: a broom LEANING in a corridor corner or a washroom (models-src/facility/janitor_build.py, render.facility.FacilityJanitor). 52 tris, 0.62 x 0.64 x 2.67, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair. ASPECT: the bristle block is 1.46 round by 0.26 tall, so the cell's full height landed on a sixth of the world height and straw drawn as vertical strands was crushed into horizontal mush -- pass v-span height/perimeter (0.18 here) and the strands stand up. PASS 6: the grey patch reported on its back was a packed-sheet bleed, and the cause is in buildlib and not here. lathe_uv TAKES u FROM atan2, WHICH IS ONLY LINEAR FOR A CIRCLE -- on a 4:1 roundrect several faces trip its max(a)-min(a) > 0.5 seam test and the t + 1.0 those get pushes u past the rect's edge; invisible on a lone cell (the sampler wraps), the NEIGHBOURING CELL on a sheet. Dumped off the built glb: the head ran to v 0.5937 where bl.cell(2) ends at 0.498, so its back really was sampling cell 0's bookbinding cloth, and the bristles ran to u 0.2877 against an R_BRISTLE ending at 0.240. Fixed with a new buildlib.shell_uv that takes u from ARC LENGTH and reads the face grid out of tube's own construction, so the seam is a real vertex boundary and nothing can land outside the rect; its swap=True does the head's quarter turn INSIDE the rect and retired janitor_build.transpose. 308 tris, unchanged. PASS 7. The block was a fifth of the prop — bristles 0.26 plus head 0.23 against a 2.67 broom — and read as a mallet. 0.17 + 0.175 now, with the shaft's foot moved 0.360 -> 0.250 and its TOP untouched so the prop still measures 2.6742 and JAN_BROOM_H does not move.

THE BAIL IS A HALF TURN FROM RIM TO RIM and the first cut got that wrong in a way worth recording -- swept through 200 degrees about a centre ON THE AXIS, both its ends landed near the middle of the bucket and it drew a hoop hanging down one side; an arc over a vessel is centred on the vessel. Its ends are pinned through the sheet just under the rim, which is what a real bail's lugs are. 0.84 tall INCLUDING the bail, which is the number render.Models.instanced scales by -- the body alone is 0.60, i.e. 0.30 m. AND IT SHIPPED INSIDE OUT, reported as 'textures inverted for body, even on the outside, horizontal lines on the inside' and it was exactly that. A CORRECTLY WOUND VESSEL CAN STILL BE INVERTED, which is the finding: the profile ran out to the rim and back down as the rule says, and every normal pointed the right way, but the return leg's radii (0.255 -> 0.290) were LARGER than the outward leg's (0.245 -> 0.285) at every height, so the surface the script called the inside was the one the room sees. Measured off the built glb, which is the only way to see it -- the band at r 0.245-0.285 wore u 0.502-0.998 (cell 3's galvanised sheet) and the band at r 0.255-0.290 wore the one-texel plain swatch. WINDING SAYS WHICH WAY A FACE LOOKS; RADIUS SAYS WHICH SIDE OF THE SHEET IT IS. Return leg pulled to 0.285 -> 0.232, a ~0.013 wall, and re-dumped: r 0.245-0.285 carries the bands, r 0.232-0.285 carries the swatch. PASS 6: the bail went THROUGH the vessel wall and the crossing showed from outside -- it arced at x-radius 0.268 with its ends at z 0.500 against a wall at 0.283 and a rod 0.022 thick. Nudging the radius cannot fix it: a half-ellipse from 0.268 hugs the taper and is still inside the wall at z 0.545. The arc now STARTS AT RIM HEIGHT, above which nothing stands wider than the return leg's 0.285, at 0.322 = the rim's 0.300 plus the rod's 0.022, so the bail touches the roll and never enters it. ITS RISE IS 0.217 AND NOT A HALF CIRCLE'S 0.322 because render.Models.instanced scales a batch by HEIGHT ALONE: swept round it measured 0.9491 against JAN_BUCKET_H 0.84 and the vessel would have come back 12% smaller to make room for its own handle. Only JAN_BUCKET_W moves, 0.60 -> 0.68 -- the bucket is now wider than it is deep, by its handle. Verified in the built glb: closest bail vertex +0.0064 outside the sheet. PASS 7. `ao` with aoReach 0.8, and the reach is the whole point: the bore is 0.5 across a span of 0.84, so at the default 0.35 the reach is 0.294 and every cross-bore ray runs out of steps — the inside of a bucket bakes as open as the outside. The return leg also gained three rings, exactly on the segment they split, because a per-vertex bake over ONE band can only draw a straight line. Bore COLOR_0 now 0.647 / 0.590 / 0.536 / 0.536 going down from the rim's 0.812. 300 -> 396 tris.

facility/desk-tray.note: THIRD PASS, REPORTED FROM THE GAME AS BRIGHT, AND IT IS THE FIRST USER OF tools/models.mjs's `gradeRect`. facility/deco-basin.note: the washroom counter, fifth and last fitting down the Blender route (models-src/facility/basin_build.py) and the strongest shape claim of the set: A BASIN IS A HOLE. The emitted version lays the bowl on the counter as a flat alpha-cut quad off sink.png and stands the tap up as a second one -- a painted dish and a painted tap, both on planes. SECOND PASS AND THE FIRST ANSWER IS SUPERSEDED. That one inset the counter's own lid, pulled it to the bowl's aspect and dropped it -- a rectangular pit with four flat walls and a flat floor at 44 tris, reported as looking poor for want of triangles, and fairly. What is here now is what the art draws: a DROP-IN SINK, lathed on a rounded rectangle (buildlib.roundrect handed to tube as its cross-section, 20 points round), with a flange that sits on the counter, a rolled rim and a tapered bowl under it -- ONE closed smooth-shaded surface running from the flange over the rim and back DOWN the inside to the floor, which is the same profile rule a mug's coffee follows. The counter gives up a HOLE under it, cut by ONE inset: it leaves the worktop flat with a hole in it and its four inner corners are then set to the hole's exact rectangle IN THE SAME PLANE, so the ring stays level rather than becoming a funnel, and that face is deleted. THIRD PASS ON THAT HOLE AND THE SHAFT IS GONE. The second pass sank a 0.07-deep shaft under the lid and CAPPED it at z 1.73 -- ABOVE the bowl's own floor at 1.200 -- so the cap cut straight across the inside of the sink and was reported from the game as a polygon covering the basin (face #10, local y 1.73, which is that number exactly). Nothing under the bowl needs closing: the vessel is one closed lathe from flange to floor, so the cap was never load-bearing, and the hole it leaves is entirely inside the flange's footprint (hole 1.12 x 0.72 against a flange reaching 1.25 x 0.775, and the bowl's widest sub-flange section 1.10 x 0.682 drops through it with 0.02 to spare). FOURTH PASS, AND THERE WAS A SECOND POLYGON ACROSS THE BASIN -- reported straight after, from the .blend rather than from the game. The BOWL'S OWN low cap: buildlib.tube closes a ring with a full DISC, and this lathe's FIRST ring is the flange's outer edge, the widest point of the whole vessel at 1.25 x 0.775. Capping it laid a 20-gon of that size at z 1.806, which is 0.07 BELOW the rim at 1.876 -- so looking over the rim you saw the sink closed off. It is the LARGEST horizontal face in the model (area 3.842 against the bowl floor's 0.346), and the pass before this one looked straight at it in a face dump and let it through because its normal points DOWN: the material is doubleSided, and a face nothing can be behind is not harmless in any case. `turned` takes cap_lo now and the bowl passes False. THE READ TO KEEP: on a profile that runs OUT and back IN over itself -- which every vessel in this repo is, the mug's coffee and the pot's soil included -- the lathe's first ring is NOT a bottom, and capping it by reflex puts a lid on the thing. A drop-in sink is open at that edge by construction, the edge being where it meets the worktop, and it sits 0.006 over a lid that overhangs it 0.13 all round; what a flange underside actually wants there is an ANNULUS, which a one-loop lathe cannot state and which nothing can see. buildlib.check reports holes 24 -- 4 boundary edges from the counter's deleted lid face and 20 from the bowl's open flange edge -- and that is the design, not a fault. THE BOWL IS SHALLOWER IN PLAN THAN SINK_BASIN_D on purpose: that constant is locked to the PAINTED basin's aspect, which the quad path lays as a picture and this mesh no longer uses at all -- what the depth has to clear here is the tap standing behind it inside BASIN_D 2.2. The bowl wears the MATERIAL off that art and not the picture: a plain uniform slice of its own basin for the walls and a darker one for the floor. THE TAP IS THE OTHER HALF -- two boxes became a turned column with a base, a swept GOOSENECK (buildlib.sweep) and a lever, which is the tap the sheet draws; it tops out at 2.8978 against BASIN_MESH_H 2.9, so the batch's scale is still 1. That also retires the family's only alpha-cut mesh: B_COUNTER and B_BASIN are the basin's ALONE and both go, while B_BASIN_TOP is shared with the benches and the partition cope and stays -- this model carries the same lid art itself. THE MIRROR STAYS A QUAD: it hangs at MIRROR_Y 3.4 against the WALL and not on the unit, and folding it in would have made the mesh 4.4 tall, which render.Models.instanced (which scales by HEIGHT alone) would then have squashed to BASIN_H, taking the counter with it. facility/bench-park-hand.note: the park bench hand-modelled instead of generated (models-src/facility/bench_build.py). 1,660 tris against the generated bench's 3,650, 1.700 x 3.5568 x 2.340, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair (buildlib.check). A BENCH IS ONE CURVE, and the first cut of this prop proved a hand-modelled thing can LOSE to the bake it replaces: it hit every locked number at 1,620 tris with holes 0 and coplanar 0, and still read worse, because it stood the back dead vertical over a flat seat on three straight boxes per end. A bake carries a curve for free and boxes do not. The nine slats are placed by ARC LENGTH on a single profile whose tangent turns -6 degrees at the seat front (a dished seat), +10 at the seat rear, 31 degrees off vertical at the foot of the back and 6 at its top -- a lumbar S -- and the curve costs ZERO triangles, each slat still being one box pitched to the tangent by a rotation about Y, the one rotation buildlib.place cannot state. The +40 tris are the frame: three straight boxes per end became two SWEPT BARS, 8-sided and smooth-shaded. DEPTH IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: a raked back travels backwards as it climbs, the profile measures 1.684 in the locked 1.700 (16 mm spare in the whole prop) and the seat run came down 1.45 to 1.008 to buy the rake; the front foot and the top rail are placed at +-(DEPTH/2 - BAR_R) by hand so depth is 1.700 by construction, with the curve centred between them by a build-time span scan behind an assert. THE BAR MUST CLEAR THE TIMBER: it rides at a constant offset along the profile's NORMAL, and 0.075 behind a 0.10-thick slat with a 0.065 radius buried it 40 mm in the wood, which reads as the slats disappearing INTO the frame; BAR_OFF 0.100 against a tangent 0.105 leaves 5 mm of bite, with BAR_R 0.065 -> 0.055 to pay the depth. And sweep SQUARES EACH RING TO THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL, so a leaning end lands a TILTED CAP -- the rear leg dug 8 mm under the floor and the top rail put the mesh 11 mm over H, which is the aspect lock broken by a cap; both feet and the rail now end on a short vertical stub. THREE NUMBERS ARE LOCKED AND NONE IS A TASTE CALL. ASPECT 1.52: FacilityStyle.PARK_BENCH_H 2.34 was fitted to the generated bench's own widest/height and Models.instanced scales by HEIGHT alone, so 2.34 x 1.52 = 3.557 is the bench length that constant's note argues for -- length is what reads from an overhead camera, at the cost of a bench standing 1.17 m rather than 0.9 m. 3.557 LONG BY 1.70 DEEP: BIN_SIDE 1.45 and BIN_BACK 1.42 are fitted against those two, because the litter bin stands off the BENCH's centre along the bench's own axes and its 0.49 radius clears the seat by 0.08 -- change the depth and the bin moves into the bench. AND IT LIES ALONG LOCAL Z FACING LOCAL +X, which is why FacilityGround.facing carries a -PI/2 for this prop: export_yup sends Blender +X to glTF +X and Blender -Y to glTF +Z, so the LENGTH is built along Blender Y, the DEPTH along Blender X, and the backrest sits at negative x with the seat front at positive. WHAT EARNS IT A MESH is the railing's own argument: a bench is SLATS, and a slat is a rhythm. The generated one reached 15 components at 35.3% and split 2.73x -- UNDECIMATABLE, the worst-conditioned of the four kerbside props -- and its whole regeneration story was about getting the gaps between the slats to come back as real openings at all, the first bake having filled them in because a grey subject on a grey backdrop gives a generator nothing to segment holes against. Stated as boxes there is nothing to segment: the gaps ARE gaps. FIVE SEAT SLATS AND FOUR BACK SLATS, the count that reference asked for in as many words, kept so the two read as the same object at the same distance. THE GRAIN RUNS ALONG THE SLAT and that needs flat_uv rather than unwrap: unwrap's widest-two guess puts u on a slat's SHORT axis, which lays the art's horizontal grain ACROSS the slat instead of down it. Every mesh slat wears ONE band of the art (v 0.270..0.355, clear of the gaps the sheet paints at 0.250 and 0.375) because they are the same slat, and picking a band per slat only risks landing a mesh slat on a painted gap. AND A SLAT HAS THREE KINDS OF FACE, NOT ONE: with v on X for every face the map is right only for the two the sitter meets, because on the long EDGES x is constant (it collapses to a single texel ROW stretched down the face) and on the ENDS y is constant (a COLUMN) -- both read as fine stripes running the wrong way round the arris. Split by face normal: +-z unchanged, +-x keeps u on the length and takes v from the THICKNESS over a v-band scaled by SLAT_T / w so a texel is the same size on the edge as on the face, and +-y, the sawn ends, take a flat two-texel patch. End grain is the one place the art cannot be turned to help -- a cut end shows rings and pores, so stripes there are wrong whichever way they run. MAP FIRST, THEN CHAMFER, and the order is forced: bmesh.ops.bevel REPLACES the faces it bevels, so touching them afterwards raises 'BMesh data of type BMFace has been removed'. It is also correct -- chamfer collects its edges before bevelling, and flat_uv is a LINEAR map over explicit ranges, so the inset corners the bevel leaves interpolate to exactly the UVs they should have. It also REORDERS the vert table, so a piece is collected by IDENTITY and never by index slice: that slice held here and did not on the office chair, where it came back carrying part of an earlier piece. No baseColor, no lift, no sat. FacilityStyle.BENCH_BLENDER switches the pair; the generated bench stays.

facility/toilet-hand.note: the WC pan hand-modelled instead of generated (models-src/facility/toilet_build.py). 652 tris against the generated pan's 4,068, 0.760 x 1.400 x 1.500, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair (buildlib.check). NEW ART: toilet-sheet.png is the left cell of a 1152x576 pack2 drawn with the chair, cut to its own native 512 -- porcelain over v 0.03..0.46, the charcoal seat over 0.52..0.73, brushed steel with two bolt heads over 0.77..0.85. No baseColor, no lift, no sat. facility/chair-hand.note: the office chair hand-modelled instead of generated (models-src/facility/chair_build.py). 1,344 tris against the generated chair's 2,930, 1.231 x 1.294 x 2.099, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair (buildlib.check). NOTHING ON A TASK CHAIR IS STRAIGHT, and the first cut of this prop was boxes with their arrises broken, which is packaging. The castors were the worst of it: they were boxes on the argument that a castor is three texels at this camera, true of ONE castor and false of five -- the base is the widest thing on the prop and its rim is the whole of what an overhead camera gets, so five square blobs read as a cross and five WHEELS read as a chair. A wheel is a lathe lying on its side, tipped by a quarter turn about x so it turns about the TANGENT, and its profile carries the tyre's crown. The arms under them are SWEPT bars carried down a path from hub to wheel, because a star base's arms sweep down and out and a box states neither half; the hub is TURNED, because it sits dead centre of the star where the camera looks straight down and a square one showed its corners between the arms; the armrests are ONE BENT BAR each rather than a pad on a post; and the seat and both back panels are ROUNDED LATHES -- roundrect carrying the plan (rounded corners on the seat, rounded ENDS on a panel) and the profile rounding the two edges the eye crosses, which is the WC pan's rim trick one prop over. A POLYGON STANDS ON ITS FLAT, NOT ON ITS RADIUS: a 10-gon's lowest vertex is R*cos(18) below centre, so wheels hung at WHEEL_R left the whole chair floating 4.2 mm off the floor. THIS IS THE CLOSEST CALL OF THE ELEVEN AND THE GAME ARGUES THE OTHER SIDE: FacilityStyle's comment on CHAIR_H says the chair is the case FOR a mesh generator -- 'a real irregular silhouette (a shaped back, arms, a five-star base on castors)'. That is right about the back and wrong about the base it names first, because FIVE ARMS AT 72 DEGREES IS THE MOST PARAMETRIC SHAPE IN THE LIST: a generator has to find the five-fold symmetry in a bake, here it is a loop index. The bake spent 2,930 tris and still came back 9 components at 61.8%, split 2.36x, a REJECT -- so the silhouette it was supposed to buy did not arrive either. THE BACK IS SPLIT AND THE REASON IS CHAIR_H: 2.1 is 1.05 m to the top of the back over a seat at 0.425 m, so there is 0.6 m of backrest to state, and as ONE panel that is geometrically right and reads as a throne. A lumbar panel, a gap and a headrest is what a task chair looks like at that height, and the gap is the part that does the work. THE MATERIAL SPLIT DOES THE JOB A UV SPLIT WOULD: the seat and the two back panels wear FABRIC on the faces a person meets and PLASTIC on the rest, which is cheaper than a three-way flat_uv and truer to the object -- fabric really does stop at the moulded shell. Which faces those are is passed in as an AXIS and never guessed: guessing upholstered the first backrest's top and bottom EDGES, a raked panel's big faces being its +-y pair. Picking them by AREA fixed the box version and cannot work on the lathe that replaced it, where the surface is fifty small quads; picking them by NORMAL against a given axis is what generalises. TWO NUMBERS CAME FROM buildlib.check: an arm of half-width 0.06 is clear of its 72-degree neighbour only outside r = 0.06 / tan(36) = 0.083, so ARM_IN 0.11 -- started at 0.05 the five arms overlapped each other near the hub and put five top faces on one plane; and BACK_W 0.58 rather than 0.62, because the lumbar panel's foot sits INSIDE the seat pad (that is the join) and at 0.62 its +-x faces ran 0.01 from the pad's own. facility/fence-park-hand.note: the park railing hand-modelled instead of generated (models-src/facility/fence_build.py), and THE ONE PROP IN THIS SET WHOSE HEIGHT IS ITS WIDTH. FacilityStyle.FENCE_H is not a chosen number, it is CityConfig.CELL / FENCE_ASPECT 2.83, and render.Models.instanced scales by HEIGHT alone -- so a segment draws exactly one cell wide only if the MESH's own width/height is exactly that aspect. Get it wrong and every run round every park gaps or overlaps at each cell boundary. Built at LEN 4.0 by LEN / 2.83, i.e. world size: measured 4.000 x 0.150 x 1.4134, aspect 2.83, so the batch's scale is 1 and neither FENCE_H nor the CLIMB_ARC 0.8 fitted against it moves. 564 tris against the generated railing's 5,056, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair (buildlib.check). THE ENDS ARE FLAT AND SQUARE AND THAT IS THE BRIEF, not a style call: two segments abut at a cell boundary, so segment A's +x post face and segment B's -x post face land on ONE PLANE -- flat and square they meet invisibly, and FrontSide culls whichever faces away because the two normals are opposed. A finial, a rounded cap or any overhang would show the join at every boundary in the park, which is why the generated one's own reference had to ask for square ends too. Verified by rendering two segments one CELL apart: no gap, and the baluster pitch 0.308 is within a hair of the 0.30 that two abutting posts make, so the rhythm carries across the join instead of stuttering at it. IT RUNS ALONG LOCAL X, because FacilityGround.fence gives an edge lying in x no turn at all and only the other two directions a quarter turn. WHAT EARNS IT A MESH is the opposite of what earns the cone one: a railing is carried by RHYTHM, not by silhouette or surface -- the balusters ARE the object, and the generated one spent 5,056 triangles on them (4 components at 86.3%, split 2.65x, UNDECIMATABLE) where stating them as eleven boxes costs a tenth of that. So the art does almost nothing and is deliberately near-uniform: one plain 16-texel swatch off fence-sheet.png, the painted steel from the kerbside pack4, SHARED WITH THE CABLE REEL -- no new art, and the two props wanting the same material is the one case where sharing a sheet file is right. Luma 48.1, the 46-52 OUTDOOR family the park stands in, so no baseColor, no lift, no sat. NO CHAMFER ON THE BALUSTERS: they are 0.06 across, an edge break there is under a texel at any camera this game has, and it would double the triangle count of the part that is already eleven boxes. The posts and the two rails get one (EDGE 0.012) because those are wide enough to catch it. FacilityStyle.FENCE_BLENDER switches the pair; the generated railing stays. PASS 2: THE SWATCH IS GREEN AND IT IS A RAILING, reported from the game as the fence reading green rather than metal. Measured on the shipped glb: atlas 41/52/47, sampled 38/51/46, chroma 10.8 / 12.4 -- green dominant over red by 11, which is the kerbside pack4's painted steel being a PAINT colour and not a zinc one. The LEVEL was right (luma in the 46-52 outdoor family, as the entry above records), so this is the bin's pass-3 finding in a smaller form: too-coloured, not too-bright. A `sat` 0.2 is the whole fix and NO NEW ART WAS GENERATED -- a fresh `facility/fence-steel` swatch was the planned route and buys nothing here, because the art is one near-uniform 16-texel patch (the balusters are geometry, the rhythm is the object) and what a zinc gen would add over a neutralised paint is mottling nothing can resolve at 0.06 across. Rec.709 in linear light holds the luma by construction, so the family fit above still stands, and the sheet is SHARED WITH THE CABLE REEL while the grade is not: `sat` bakes into this label's own copy of the map, so facility/lot-reel-hand is untouched and stays painted steel in its parking lot. NOT VERIFIED IN FRAME AND THAT IS A LIMIT OF THE SCENE, not an omission: this game is permanently night, the park is the darkest part of the compound, and three pinned free-cam frames on lamp-lit rim cells came back at mean luma 10 with the railing either occluded by shrubs or under a texel of light -- the albedo is the only instrument that reads here, and it is the one the report is about.

facility/lot-cone-hand.note: STRAIGHTER, WITH A ROUND TIP. Reported against the first cut's convex shell, which is a nose cone and not a road cone. The first five rings now sit exactly on one line, r = 0.300 - 0.1807 * (z - CONE_SLAB), so every band below z 1.35 is a true frustum; only the last three leave it, slope going 0.21 -> 0.40 -> 0.70 to turn the shoulder over into a 0.014 apex where the old one stopped flat at 0.045. 392 tris against 360, 0.760 x 0.760 x 1.500, z_min 0, holes 0, coplanar 0. facility/lot-reel-hand.note: SAT 0.2 AND A REAL PIECE OF THE SHEET. Reported as the reel having no difference in texture anywhere and being GREEN. Both were true and they are separate faults. The green is the shared fence-sheet.png, which is the kerbside pack4's PAINTED steel at rgb 41/52/47, green over red by 11 -- the same measurement the railing took a Rec.709 sat 0.2 for, and since that bakes into each label's own copy of the map, the reel needs its own. The flatness was structural: every FLAT ANNULUS on this lathe, which is the whole of what this camera looks at, wore a 16 x 16 crop of an already near-uniform sheet stretched over 2.66 units, and the turned bands wore R_FULL -- the whole sheet, rail highlight included, as a stripe round a 0.1-tall rim. Both now take the sheet's clean field (u 0.05..0.95, v 0.26..0.96, std 5.5 over a mean of 46/52/47), stopping short of that highlight at v 0.148..0.21. the empty cable reel in the parking lot hand-modelled instead of generated (models-src/facility/lot_build.py), and THE ENTRY HERE IS THAT IT IS ONE LATHE. A cable reel LOOKS like an assembly -- two flanges, a barrel, a hub at each end -- and the generated one came back as six components trying to be exactly that (propstat REJECT, largest 44.5%). It is nothing of the kind: the whole object is a single (radius, z) table turned once, running out along the bottom face, over the rim, back in to the barrel, along it, and out again to the top flange. CCW round the section the whole way, which is checkable segment by segment: travel direction rotated -90 degrees in (r, z) has to point OUT of the solid. 676 tris against 4,960, 2.660 x 2.660 x 2.400, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair. IT STANDS AXIS-UP AND THAT IS READ OFF THE OLD GLB, not chosen: its bbox is 0.999 x 0.901 x 0.999 -- two EQUAL horizontal extents and a shorter height -- which is a reel resting on a flange FACE, not one lying on its rims. The first build laid it on its rims and it read as a dumbbell. Axis-up needs no rotation at all, and REEL_R 1.33 against LOT_REEL_H 2.4 reproduces the old aspect 1.109 to three places. THE BANDS ARE UV-MAPPED SEPARATELY AND THAT IS THE POINT OF SPLITTING THEM: a flange face is a FLAT ANNULUS and goes through disc_uv, radially, where lathe_uv would put the seam on a radius and converge every wedge on the axis -- the bin's lid wedge in another shape. The turned bands (rims, chamfers, barrel, rib and hub rims) take lathe_uv over the whole sheet on one continuous v up the axis, and only those are shaded smooth. THE TOP FACE IS WHAT THIS CAMERA LOOKS AT: 2.66 across and, in the first build, one flat tone with nothing for the light to catch, so it gained a stiffening RIB and a raised HUB -- two more rings in the table, +80 tris, and what a real drum flange has anyway. NO NEW ART: it wears fence-sheet.png, the painted steel drawn in the kerbside pack4 at luma 48.1, which is the 46-52 OUTDOOR family the lot wants and level with what the generated reel shipped at after its baseColor 0.19. No baseColor, no lift, no sat. THIS PROP IS ALSO WHY buildlib.check GREW A REAL OVERLAP TEST: it reported 136 coplanar pairs at gap 0, every one a pair of wedges two to four sectors apart in the same flat annulus, whose axis-aligned BOUNDING BOXES overlap while the wedges never touch. _overlaps is a separating-axis test now. facility/trash-bin-hand.note: the park litter bin hand-modelled instead of generated (models-src/facility/bin_build.py), and THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE SINGLE PROP IN THE COMPOUND: one instanced batch serves the park (one bin per bench), the corridor dead ends and every FIT_BIN floor fitting, so one mesh is three populations and FacilityStyle.DECO_ROUND_H is BIN_H. 668 tris against the generated bin's 4,765, 0.970 x 0.970 x 1.800, z_min 0, holes 0 and no near-coplanar pair (buildlib.check). THE MOUTH IS A HOLE NOW AND THAT IS THE SECOND CUT OF THIS PROP. The first stated the bin as the art does -- one green can wearing a wrap with the litter mouth PAINTED on it, the mouth landing wherever the seam put that paint. It measures well and it is wrong, because a painted mouth has no depth and the one thing a litter bin IS, is a hole. The reference the generator worked from draws the shape properly and the rebuild follows it: a CHARCOAL HOOD over the top quarter rather than a domed lid the colour of the body (most of what makes the prop read as a litter bin and not a drum at forty tiles), a REAL LETTERBOX SLOT through that hood's wall four of sixteen sectors wide, and the green ribbed body below. THE SLOT GOES THROUGH THE WALL, SO IT IS MISSING FROM BOTH SURFACES: cutting it out of the outer wall alone left the sill and the lintel meeting an inner wall that was still whole -- three faces on one edge, ten non-manifold edges, and a mouth sealed shut by a skin you cannot see. With both cut, the eye goes in and lands on the FAR INNER wall, which is where the depth comes from. The hood is built ring by ring rather than with tube, because a lathe cannot miss out four sectors of one band, and its winding is not reasoned about at all -- recalc_face_normals takes a closed shell and points every face out, which is one call against sixteen chances to get a quad backwards. AND THE HOOD'S GREY WAS MEASURED OFF THE REFERENCE, not guessed: trash-bin-src.png draws the hood at luma 75.4 against the body's 72.9, ratio 1.035, i.e. THE SAME VALUE -- it reads as dark because it is NEUTRAL beside a green, not because it is darker. Guessing it darker (44.5, ratio 0.58) took the prop's sampled level from 68 to 48 against the generated bin's effective 78. The slot's lining is the one thing that really is darker, at the reference's own ratio 0.588. Both swatches are PAINTED INTO THE PART OF THE SHEET NOTHING READS ANY MORE: with the mouth in geometry the body wraps only the lower 60% of the art, which leaves the old painted mouth and the old rim band dead, so the hood's neutral costs no second file and no second texture bind. SEAM 0.75 AND NOT 0.7726, which the first cut needed and this one does not: the seam existed to land the painted mouth on +Z, and with the mouth in the geometry its only job is to hide itself at the BACK. The one it replaces is a propstat REJECT on its own gate -- 2 components at 58.2% -- and its colour took three separate corrections to settle, which is the case for a CELL OF A SHEET over a bake: the trash-bin entry beside this one records a per-channel baseColor that drove a 20.1-chroma bottle-green body to 0.1 and shipped it grey, then a level refit after the interior repaint. THE SLOT IS CENTRED ON LOCAL +Z and that is measured, not chosen: FacilityGround.bins yaws by `look + PI/2` and the old glb's mouth was found on +z by binning its lid band's area by azimuth. export_yup sends Blender -Y to glTF +Z, i.e. theta = -pi/2 = 270 degrees, and sector i of sixteen spans i*22.5 degrees, so sectors 10..13 span 225..315 and centre on 270 exactly -- which is also why sixteen sides is the right count here and not the drum's twenty, four sectors being 90 degrees on the nose. R_MAX 0.485: BIN_SIDE 1.45 and BIN_BACK 1.42 are fitted to the bin's RADIUS against the bench's half-extents with 0.08 to spare, and BIN_H 1.8 to the old glb's aspect 0.54, so the mesh is built AT world size (aspect 0.539) and the batch's scale stays 1 -- not one placement constant moves. A SWATCH THROUGH lathe_uv IS THIS MODEL'S OWN FINDING and still governs both flat colours: u runs once across the rect and the seam lays the swatch's left edge against its right, so a 16-texel patch arrives as a hard line up the piece -- collapse the rect to ONE TEXEL and there is no width for a seam to be across. THE SHEET IS A CROP AND THAT DEPARTS FROM drum_build DELIBERATELY: bin, bench, fence and cone were drawn in ONE 1k gen as a 2x2, because drawing a family side by side is what makes it agree, but the three drums share one MESH and differ only by cell where these four share nothing and use one cell each. Shipping the packed sheet would hand every glb a 512 texture it uses a quarter of, so the cells are cut to their own native 512 files -- same bytes, four times the texels. Generated packed, shipped cropped. Prompted against style_prop and not style, the drums' own call: a bottle-green bin has to read GREEN, and style's 'very dark and muted desaturated palette' clause is the documented way nine props here shipped grey. THIRD CUT: THE CAN IS OPEN AND THE MOUTH HAD TWO FAULTS, BOTH GEOMETRY. Reported in game as 'the hole exposes bad polygon work - just flat surface that's not even black + green parts coming up a little too high and are visible'. The second cut capped the body at the collar and tagged that cap dark, which put a HORIZONTAL DISC 0.028 under the sill filling the whole slot: one plane, one normal, one value -- and a horizontal face takes more ambient than any wall around it, so the darkest texel on the sheet still rendered LIGHTER than the charcoal framing it. No texture fixes that. The collar also stood 0.020 PROUD of AP_Z0, so a strip of the body's GREEN ran along the bottom of the hole, which is the one colour that must never appear inside one. Fixed by carrying the profile OVER the collar's lip and back down a throat to a floor 0.8 m below (buildlib.tube's vessel rule, the same one the WC pan runs), and by dropping COLLAR_TOP to 1.412, under the sill. The throat's bands are UV'd SEPARATELY and that is forced, not tidy: one lathe_uv over the whole profile puts v on z, and the throat runs back down through the z the body already used, so it would come back wearing the ribbed green a second time, mirrored, inside the hole. AND THE THROAT IS DARKER THAN THE MOUTH, at luma 23.4 against the lining's 44.5 -- 0.31 of the hood where the reference's slot interior is 0.57 of its hood side. That 0.57 is a RATIO measured off a reference carrying its own ambient; what the game draws is a shaft down a closed can with no baked AO anywhere on a hand-made prop. Two values inside one hole is what stops it reading as the painted rectangle this rebuild exists to replace. +96 tris. FacilityStyle.BIN_BLENDER switches the two paths; the generated bin stays. PASS 7: baked AO. `ao` is FITTED so the bake costs 20% of the prop's LEVEL and no more (mean COLOR_0 = 0.80, one step from `ao * 0.20 / (1 - mean)`), because every prop here was value-fitted and a flat 0.55 drops some of them 37%. Shipped ao 0.38, aoReach 0.5. PASS 3: THE BODY WAS THE LOUDEST THING IN THE SHED AND IT WAS NOT ITS LEVEL, reported from the hangar as the can being too bright and asked as an albedo question. Measured in the frame it stands in: body 9.6/48.3/21.9, luma 26.6 against the floor beside it at 28.0 and the steel drum next to it at 43.5 -- so the LEVEL was already right and the CHROMA was 38.7, the second loudest in frame after the yellow biohazard drum's 47.8, in a compound lit blue throughout. The sheet says the same: rows 200..512 are the ribbed body at 50/87/51, chroma 37, where the charcoal hood above them is 73/76/77 at chroma 4. NEITHER `baseColor` NOR `sat` CAN STATE THAT: a flat factor darkens a hood that measures correctly, a per-channel one tints it magenta, and a whole-map `sat` is the closest of the three but still pulls the only neutral part of the prop. `gradeRect` is the instrument for exactly this -- one prop, one sheet, two surfaces -- so the grade is the green band alone at scale 0.82 and sat 0.42, which takes the body to 57/69/57, chroma 12, level with wild/bench-park-hand's accepted 12.2. The hood is not touched.

facility/drum-steel-hand.note: THE WRAP NOW CLOSES AND GOES ROUND TWICE. (2) A cell is SQUARE and an unrolled drum is 2 pi R / H = 2.09 : 1, so one wrap spent 136 texels per world unit across the barrel against 284 up it and the signs came back 2.09x wider than tall. WRAPS 2 lands 291 against 282, isotropic to 3%, and puts a round sign on each side. It costs no seam now that the cell closes, and 2 divides SIDES 20 as lathe_uv requires. buildlib's `reps` had to be fixed first -- its copy index was a ROUNDED minimum, exact only at reps == turn count, and at reps 2 over 20 sides face 5 slid a whole copy (measured u 0.0..0.2 where the face spans 0.5..0.6). floor is the copy. It certified the steel cell as the neutral the other two were being brought to -- 'at chroma 72.8 and luma 60.1 it is already the thing the other two are being brought to' -- and the cell measures rgb 23.7/66.2/108.1, CHROMA 84.4 (tools/pix.py models-src/facility/drum-sheet.png --box steel,4,4,508,508). That is not steel, it is a BLUE DRUM, and after both siblings were graded it was the loudest surface of the three: 84.4 against bio's 74.9 and rad's 45.3. The first shipped a twelve-sided flat-shaded can at 44 tris and read as exactly that; the argument for twelve ('eight show their flats, sixteen buys nothing') was sound and its premise was wrong -- FLAT SHADING SPENDS EVERY SIDE ON THE SURFACE, so twelve was the point where facets stopped reading, and buildlib.finish was forcing every polygon flat. It also has a PROFILE now (buildlib.tube turns a (radius, z) table): a rolled chime at each end and two ROLLING HOOPS, placed on the v where the wrap art draws its own bead lines -- measured off the sheet's vertical gradient, rows 113-139 and 325-352 of 512, so the pressed steel and the painted steel are the same hoop. The frame is still three rails and two uprights, now with every arris broken (buildlib.chamfer, EDGE 0.012, and the strips take a plain slice of the frame cell rather than the whole plate of rivets).
