BAKED AO INSTEAD OF A RIM LINE, and that is the whole of pass 6's second look at this prop. Four bottles 0.096 apart read as one orange slab because nothing in the lighting can separate two vertical faces: IndoorMask's only directional term is 1 + bounce * dot(N, up), the hemisphere keys on normal.y alone and there is no camera-side fill in the rig. A view-space contour term was built, fitted live and REJECTED on looks - too bright and visibly pixelated at the rig's distance, because past pow 24 the line goes sub-pixel and dots, and under it the line is a wash. AO is the term that darkens a place because of the SHAPE around it, it costs the frame nothing (COLOR_0 multiplies in three's own shader) and the gap between two bottles is exactly what it can see. aoRes 128 and not the default 72: the voxel cell is span/res, so at 72 over a 3.0-unit span a cell is 0.042 and the 0.096 gap is two cells wide - the crevice the term exists for would be resolved by the grid's own error. 128 puts 4 cells in it.

facility/drum-steel.note: THREE LABELS OFF ONE SOURCE MESH — this, facility/drum-bio and facility/drum-rad are the SAME glb as sewer/drum, repainted. The low decoration list holds three distinct barrels (entities64 12/1 grey with a hazard triangle, 12/2 yellow biohazard, 12/5 red radioactive) and render.facility.FacilityDeco draws one kind per livery, so each is its own label, its own path and therefore its own instanced batch — render.Models.instanced is keyed by path and there is no per-instance UV offset, so a livery costs a draw call and there is no way around that. NO NEW MESH AND NO TRELLIS RUN: the drum was already correct as a shape, and only its paint was wrong (reported as 'it's a dirty sewers drum'). AN edit_image PASS WAS THE PLAN AND WAS REJECTED ON INSPECTION: a TRELLIS base map is a fragmented UV ATLAS — circular lid/base charts scattered through rectangular body panels — and an image model regenerates the whole canvas rather than preserving chart boundaries to the texel (docs/3d-textures.md records it refusing to honour even a stated seam position), so a chart that moves a few texels is a smeared prop. tools/livery.py does it as a per-pixel HSV transform instead, which cannot move a texel by construction. ONE OPERATION COVERS BOTH JOBS, and that is a property of this particular bake: the rust and the steel have nearly the same LUMA (54/44/42 against 44/47/54) and differ only in HUE — 17% of saturated texels at hue 0-30 against 71% at 210-240 — so assigning ONE hue to every saturated texel deletes the grime and applies the livery at once, while the untouched value channel keeps the dents and weld seams reading as wear. Near-neutral texels (SAT_MIN 0.12: the dark lid rims and baked contact shadows) are left alone, or the shadows would take the paint. Built with --hue 212 --sat 0.22 --gain 1.63 and carries NO baseColor: the gain lands the atlas at 72.6/79.4/87.3, luma 78.5, which IS the shipped albedo. 78 is the indoor number facility/lab-trolley and facility/gas-cylinders both record — the 46-52 family was fitted OUTDOORS against asphalt, and after the interior repaint the room floor's albedo is 95 and the wall's 111, so a prop at 49 renders as a hole. dropMR because propstat reads the source at metallic 1 with an MR map whose metal max is 168; it only fails to render black because Models.toLambert drops the PBR path, and stripping it also drops a texture the Lambert path never samples. tris 1200 IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS GOT WRONG ONCE: propstat on the BUILT sewer drum reads split 2.53x and prints 'UNDECIMATABLE, generate AT the budget with tris -1', which is advice about the 4,826-tri thing it was handed and NOT about the source — models-src/sewer/drum.glb is the 100k MASTER, so -1 built a 97,214-tri drum. sewer/drum's own 1200 is what meshopt floors to 4,826, and copying it is what makes these three the same mesh as the tunnels' drum with only the paint changed. READ A propstat LINE AGAINST THE FILE IT WAS RUN ON.

facility/drum-bio.note: the YELLOW BIOHAZARD barrel (entities64 12/2). One of three liveries off one source mesh — the whole derivation, and why an edit_image pass was rejected for a per-pixel HSV transform, is on facility/drum-steel. Built with --hue 48 --sat 0.62 --gain 1.85: atlas 99.2/88.4/52.6, chroma 46.6, luma 88.1, no baseColor. Chroma 46.6 is well over propstat's 'a coloured prop wants > 25' and is the whole point of the exercise — the sibling it replaces shipped at 6.3. It is the BRIGHTEST of the three on purpose: a hazard yellow that is not brighter than the steel drum beside it is not a hazard yellow, and 88 is still inside the indoor band the trolley's note fixes at ~78. NO SYMBOL IS PAINTED ON IT and that is a size call, not an oversight: the drum stands DECO_ROUND_H 1.8 world units and draws around 40 screen pixels at the resting camera, where a trefoil is about 8 px and the atlas is fragmented across charts with no way to know which one faces the room. The COLOUR is the read at that size, which is also how the 2D icons separate at a glance. SAT 0.5 SINCE, with facility/gas-cylinders and for its reason — reported as too bright and colourful. MEASURED atlas chroma 46.6 -> 19.1, sampled 42.6 -> 17.4, which is deliberately UNDER propstat's > 25 line: that line is advice for a prop whose colour has to carry it outdoors, and 'the brightest of the three' above is a statement about the RANK rather than about the level. The two coloured drums do NOT come out level, and that is the mix and not a mis-fit: they went in at 45.9 and 45.5 and came out at 19.1 and the rad drum's 23.7, because the Rec.709 weights put 72% of luminance in green, so a yellow (95/89/76) loses more of its spread to its own luminance than a red (92/70/69) does. LUMA is what carries this drum's 'brightest of the three' and luma is untouched. And the livery's own --sat 0.62 is left alone: halving at the bake is one key in one place, where re-running tools/livery.py re-derives the base map.

facility/drum-rad.note: the RED RADIOACTIVE barrel (entities64 12/5), and the commonest of the three on a generated compound — 3 of the 4 drums this seed deals. One of three liveries off one source mesh; the derivation is on facility/drum-steel. Built with --hue 6 --sat 0.58 --gain 1.97: atlas 105.9/62.7/59.6, chroma 46.3, luma 71.7, no baseColor. It takes the HIGHEST gain of the three and still lands the LOWEST luma, which is not a mis-fit but what red is: at hue 6 the green and blue channels carry almost none of the luminance, so the same value multiplier buys far less brightness than it does at the yellow's hue 48. Left there rather than pushed to match — a red drum brighter than the yellow one beside it would read as orange. SAT 0.5 SINCE, with the other two and for facility/gas-cylinders' reason: MEASURED atlas chroma 45.5 -> 23.7, sampled 42.4 -> 22.0. facility/drum-steel is the one of the three that did NOT take the key — measured at chroma 15.0 it is a blue-grey steel drum already, and halving that is a dead neutral rather than a muted one.

facility/roof-ac-hand.note: THE ROOFTOP CONDENSER, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofac_build.py) behind render.facility.FacilityStyle.ROOF_BLENDER, 660 tris against the TRELLIS bake's 5,619. The bake's own note argues correctly that a condenser is carried by the FAN GUARD in its top face and not by its outline -- the camera pitches 51 degrees down -- but that is an argument against a BOX EMITTER, which has no art for that face. It is not an argument for 5,619 triangles: the guard is a disc of art and the well round it is a lathe, and both are numbers. Measured on the EVALUATED mesh at 2.7775 x 1.77 x 2.2, z_min 0, buildlib.check 0 holes / 0 coplanar. THE HEIGHT IS THE ONLY DIMENSION THE GAME STATES (Models.instanced scales by height alone), so the prop is built AT 2.2 and draws at exactly its built plan size -- 2.78 in a 4.0 cell, squarer than the bake's 3.16 x 1.86, which was the generator's aspect and not the object's. THE FAN WELL IS A RAISED COWL AND NOT A HOLE: a box has no hole in its lid and cutting one leaves check() a hole at every cut edge, so the ring wall stands ON the lid with the guard PLATE (not a disc -- a single flat polygon is a boundary edge all the way round) set 0.06 down inside it. The cowl was 0.72 deep on the first build and read as a duct standing on a box; 0.34 is a lip. THE LOUVRE IS ART AND THE FRAME IS GEOMETRY: a bank of real slats is 6 quads each and would spend the whole budget on the one face that already has a fitted texture, so two proud rails give the flank its lit top and bottom edge for 24 quads. AND THE LOUVRE CELL TAKES A WINDOW OF ITSELF: 114 slats measured across the 512 cell (4.5 px pitch), which laid whole over a 1.2-unit flank is 95 slats per world unit -- a slat every 5 mm at the half-metre unit WALL_H 6.0 fixes, i.e. mush. A 0.12 v-window is 13 slats, a slat every 9 cm. Sheet fitted by models-src/facility/rooftone.py to the props it replaces: propstat --audit reads the bakes at srgb 45.3 (dish) and 47.6 (condenser), so the four cells take gammas 1.11 / 1.46 / 1.23 / 1.53 onto 0.020 / 0.036 / 0.028 / 0.036 linear and the sheet lands at 0.0300 / 48.0. No baseColor -- the fit is in the pixels.

facility/roof-dish-hand.note: THE ROOFTOP COMMS DISH, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofdish_build.py) behind ROOF_BLENDER, 948 tris against the TRELLIS bake's 5,800. This is the textbook case for the fourth route: that bake took two references, the first coming back 20 components at 74.4% (every strut its own island, every gap real air) and the fix was to repaint the object as ONE SOLID LUMP -- i.e. to ask the generator for less of the thing that makes a dish a dish. THE SECTION IS A REAL PARABOLOID, z = r^2 / (4f), and the focal ratio is the one number a dish has: f / D = 0.40, the middle of the real prime-focus band, so at D 2.66 the focus is 1.064, the depth follows as R^2/(4f) = 0.4156 and the feed horn stands AT the focus rather than at a styled height. Measured 2.66 x 1.809 x 3.6 exactly (MAST_H is solved against the tilted rim, ELEV 40 degrees), z_min 0, 0 holes / 0 coplanar. ONE LATHE AND ONE CLOSED SOLID: up the back from a 0.06 vertex annulus to the rim, across the rim, down the concave front and home -- buildlib.tube's vessel rule, where ascending legs take outward normals and descending ones inward, which is exactly right for a shell. BOTH FACES ARE MAPPED RADIALLY and not wrapped: their art IS a disc (radial panel joints on the front cell, radial stiffening ribs on the back), so disc_uv puts the art's circle on the mesh's circle -- the drum-lid finding. A lathe wrap would run those joints round the rim. STEPS PAYS FOR SIDES: 5 rings up a smooth-shaded parabola read the same as 6 while 16 sides read as a polygon at this aperture, so 5 x 20 costs the same 220 bands as 6 x 16 did. FIRST BUILD REPORTED 2 COPLANAR PAIRS: the pivot's end caps landed 0.010 outside the yoke plates' own outer faces, exactly on check()'s `near` -- the overhang is 1.6 x YOKE_W now. Sheet fitted by rooftone.py: gammas 2.85 / 1.98 / 2.28 / 1.14 onto 0.040 / 0.032 / 0.033 / 0.026 linear, sheet 0.0328 / srgb 53.6 against the bake's 45.3. The painted face came back at 0.3225 -- 11.7x the deck it stands on -- which is what a fresh gen does and why none of these ship raw.

facility/roof-hatch-hand.note: THE ROOF ACCESS HATCH, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofhatch_build.py) 56 tris. NOT behind ROOF_BLENDER, unlike the condenser and the dish: that flag switches between two glbs of one object, and this replaces merged geometry the game asked to be rid of, so there is nothing to switch to. IT LEFT A QUAD EMITTER THAT COST NO DRAW CALL, which the box-vs-silhouette test alone cannot justify -- a hatch IS a box. The fault was the ART: as merged geometry it wore facility/booth-roof at ROOF_TILE 9.0, i.e. a ninth of a kiosk roof's standing seam on each face, and the game reported that twice (a box of coping, then a reused texture). A 1.2 x 1.0 m lid's whole read is the tread plate ON it seen from a camera that pitches 51 to 86 degrees down, and a plate pattern is a PICTURE of a lid: it maps 0..1 onto that one face, which a world-aligned tiling emitter cannot do. Built at HATCH_CURB + HATCH_LID = 0.4 exactly, so render.Models.instanced's height scale is 1 and the 2.4 x 2.0 plan the generator's cells are sized against is the built plan. Its own 1k sheet, four cells for four surfaces (tread lid / curb elevation / drip band / galvanised), toned by rooftone.py to 47.9 srgb. No ao: there is no concavity on a lipped lid, and 56 tris of box is exactly what a baked occlusion map has nothing to say about.

facility/roof-jbox-hand.note: THE ROOFTOP ISOLATOR CABINET, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofjbox_build.py) 88 tris -- the box every group of condensers is wired back to (FacilityRoof.runs). Same trade as facility/roof-hatch-hand and the same cause: it wore booth-roof too, and the report on it was two words long -- don't reuse textures. A cabinet's read is its LOUVRE BANK and its latch, which is a picture of a door and has to map 0..1 onto it. Built at ROOF_JBOX_H 0.9 with the 0.75 x 0.55 plan the emitter used, so the height scale is 1. SCALE is the HEIGHT and not a plan axis: the door is the tallest face, so at 0.9 it takes 83% of its cell across and 94% up and the louvre bank lands intact. Its own 1k sheet, four cells (louvred door / side panel / lid with gland plate / galvanised), toned to 47.3 srgb.

facility/deco-pallet-rack.note: THE STORE ROOM'S RACKING, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/storerack_build.py) 428 tris -- four uprights, three beam levels, a braced end frame each side, foot plates and a timber deck on EVERY level. THREE DECKS AND NOT ONE, and the foot plate CENTRED on its own post: the first build decked only the bottom beam pair and inset the plates 0.02 inside the post plane to hold the stated width, and both came back off the game as faults -- "why no second shelf" and "you sure this should not be centered around the strut instead". The plate is now what measures RACK_W (the post centre is solved back from it) so both are true at once. AND THE TWO NARROW MEMBERS MOVE THE FIT'S WINDOW OFF THE CELL'S CENTRE (buildlib.at), to the flattest 48 px band by luma std. At tex 512 a cell is 256 px and the post's 0.14 face is EIGHT TEXELS wide, so it can hold a colour and not a picture: the fit centred on the cell put the punched keyhole column on every post as a smeared ribbon, and the whole cell framed onto the face (tried and rejected) made it one black slit at 30:1. CUTTING THE RECT FIRST WAS WORSE THAN EITHER and is the fault the anchor replaced -- the fit crops whatever rect it is handed by faceExtent / scale, so a pre-cut 56 px band times the beam's own 3.8% came out a TWO PIXEL sliver stretched along 3.6 units, reported straight back from the game. Its arrises take the post's OWN rect -- they were galvanised against an orange upright, which outlined every post in grey. Built at DECO_PALLET_RACK_H 4.2, the tallest fitting in the compound (the cabinet is 3.43), which is what makes the store's AISLE zone necessary: racking blocks sight as well as movement. 3.9 WIDE AND NOT 4.0, which is the one number here with a fault behind it: a run of racking is one instance per CELL and a cell is CityConfig.CELL 4.0, so a cell-wide rack abuts the next one EXACTLY -- two coincident faces and a z-fight between instances rather than a continuous bay. 3.9 leaves a 0.1 shadow gap that reads as the joint between two bays. Its own 1k sheet, four cells (punched upright / painted beam / pallet timber / galvanised), toned by storetone.py to the INDOOR band and not the outdoor one -- and with its TIMBER CELL TURNED A QUARTER in the same pass, because buildlib.frame puts u on a flat face's longest edge and the gen drew its planks running up the cell, so a 3.6-long deck board wore its grain across itself: ~78 srgb, because the compound's interior is a floor at 95 and a wall at 111 and an outdoor prop indoors reads as a black card.

facility/deco-pallet-stack.note: A SHRINK-WRAPPED PALLET OF CARTONS, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/storerack_build.py) 116 tris -- the cheapest of the store's three and the one that says the room is in use. A pallet is three deck boards across three full-length STRINGERS and no bottom boards -- the first build put three 0.32 blocks on the centre line and it was reported straight back as "the foundation is incorrect, three small blocks", which from any side showed a single stump under a 1.8-wide deck. Three runners is the same three boxes and reads right from every hand. What is seen of a pallet at this camera is its top and the slot of shadow under it: what is seen of one at this camera is its top and the slot of shadow under it. The block above it is ONE box with its lid on a different cell from its flanks, which is the per-face rule read as art -- the side is two courses of carton behind creased film and the top is carton lids with a taped seam and a shipping label. Built at DECO_PALLET_STACK_H 1.5, 1.8 square in plan.

facility/deco-drum-pallet.note: A PALLET OF FOUR DRUMS, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/storerack_build.py) 376 tris. IT DOES NOT REUSE THE SHIPPED drum-*-hand GLBS, which the plan assumed it would: render.Models.instanced keeps the FIRST mesh of a glb and drops the rest silently, so a pallet carrying separate drum meshes is a pallet carrying one drum. They are lathed into the same mesh instead, 10 sides each with the rolling hoops drawn as a radius that CHANGES rather than as a decal. Its three side bands share ONE cell base to lid rather than each fitting its own slice of it: asked separately, a 6 cm rolling hoop gets a window as tall as itself about the CELL'S CENTRE, which on this sheet is the hazard diamond -- so both hoops wore a sliver of the symbol the body between them was already wearing whole, and the game reported it. The profile's z runs straight onto the cell's v instead (lathe_uv's v0/v1), so the drum wears the picture of a drum once. The lid is mapped RADIALLY (buildlib.disc_uv, the drum-lid finding): its cell IS a picture of a closing ring and two bungs seen from above, which is the angle this compound's camera looks at a pallet from. Built at DECO_DRUM_PALLET_H 1.4, 1.8 square in plan, on the same three-stringer pallet the stack wears; its own 1k sheet came off the gen at 0.0156 linear -- 5x DARKER than the indoor band wants -- so storetone.py's gammas here are below 1 where every roof gamma is above it.

facility/roof-vent-hand.note: THE ROOF EXTRACT VENT, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofsvc_build.py) 172 tris -- a mushroom cowl on a curb, the smallest of the three new service families. ONE SHEET FOR THREE PROPS (models-src/facility/roof-svc-sheet.png, toned by rooftone.py to 0.0280 linear / 49.5 srgb): the vent, the duct and the tank are one material family, and each of the four cells is the DOMINANT face of a different one of them, so a single 1k gen carried the lot at a quarter of three solo sheets. THE COWL IS MAPPED RADIALLY AND NOT WRAPPED: cell 0's art IS a disc (radial ribs out of a pressed centre ring), which is what a mushroom vent reads as under a camera pitching 51 to 86 degrees down, so every sloping band of the cap goes through disc_uv and only the rim -- the one band at constant radius, where a radial projection collapses to a line -- is lathe-wrapped. Built at ROOF_VENT_H 1.1 exactly, 0.8 x 0.8 in plan, z_min 0, 0 holes / 0 coplanar.

facility/roof-duct-hand.note: ONE CELL OF LAGGED DUCT ON ITS SADDLE, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofsvc_build.py) 220 tris. IT IS BUILT AT EXACTLY ONE CELL LONG, 4.0, and that is the whole reason a duct can be a prop rather than a swept mesh: render.Models.instanced scales a glb by HEIGHT alone, so a segment built at its stated height draws its stated length and segments dropped on neighbouring cell centres abut with no seam and no per-instance scale -- a run is N placements in a row for one draw call. ROOF_DUCT_H 1.0 IS SOLVED AGAINST THE FLANGE and not the jacket: the three flange rings are the widest thing on the segment, so the axis sits at H - flange radius and the height scale stays 1. The lagging's straps run ACROSS its cell, i.e. at constant v, and lathe_uv runs v along the lathe's axis -- so they come out as rings round the duct rather than as stripes down it. Measured 4.0 x 0.72 x 1.0, z_min 0, 0 holes / 0 coplanar.

facility/roof-tank-hand.note: THE ROOF EXPANSION TANK, HAND-MODELLED (models-src/facility/roofsvc_build.py) 236 tris -- a painted vessel on four legs with a drain stub off its shoulder. Shares the service kit's sheet; cell 3 (painted plate, one weld seam, a stencilled ring and a rust bloom) is its dominant face and takes the top of the band at 0.029 linear. THE SHOULDER IS A RADIUS THAT CHANGES and not a cone: buildlib.tube's own argument, and at this camera the two steps catching light are what says vessel rather than drum. THE LEGS RUN UP INTO THE SHELL, 0.08 past its base disc -- a leg top level with that disc is two co-facing planes at zero distance, which is exactly buildlib.check's shared-plane fault. Built at ROOF_TANK_H 1.6, 0.92 across the shell (the bbox reads 1.12 because the drain stub leaves it), z_min 0, 0 holes / 0 coplanar.

facility/hangar-podium.note: THE HANGAR'S STUDY PODIUM, hand-modelled (models-src/facility/podium_build.py) because every number in it is one the generator already committed to: gen.blocks.HangarBlock carves a PAD_SZ x PAD_SZ square of unwalkable concrete at the centre of the shed and stands four machine banks two cells clear of its edge, so the dais radius and the emitter ring are fixed by the pad, not chosen. Measured on the EVALUATED mesh at 540 tris, 17.2 x 17.2 x 3.07, z_min 0, buildlib.check 0 holes / 0 coplanar. ONE LATHE for both steps and the tread between them, so the piece is a closed solid — a lower step with a lid and an upper step with a floor is two discs in one plane, which is what shipped both server racks full of holes. THREE SHEET CELLS ON ONE PIECE, per the per-face rule: port band on the lower riser where the cables go in, tread plate on the tread and the upper lid, bolted panel on the upper riser. tex 1024 AND NOT 512: at 512 each packed cell is 256 px and the tread disc is 17.2 units across, which is 15 texels/unit against facility/floor-tile's 73. At 1024 the cell is 512 and modelsheet baked 3x3 repeats into it, so the tread lands at ~89. No baseColor/lift/sat — the four labels carry their own fitted lifts and all four built to sRGB 63. EMISSIVE IS HAND-PAINTED (models-src/facility/podium_emissive.py) AND NOT RAYCAST. tools/emissive.py exists for a TRELLIS atlas, where no one can tell by looking which patch is the lamp lens; a hand-modelled prop is the opposite case — buildlib put the eight columns on a KNOWN cell of a known sheet and `unwrap` maps each column's height up that cell's v, so the band is a rectangle that can simply be stated. Raycasting it instead came back as a 238-texel hairline on the cell seam, three boxes running. The band is 0.08..0.26 down the column at strength 2.0 against the guard booth's glazing at 1.4: a band on a matte column rather than a whole lit pane. THE TRAP WHILE CHECKING IT: moveTo over CDP does not rebuild the player's FOV, so the shed stays unlit and an emissive that works looks broken — Game.turn() is what lights it. PASS 2: THE DECK PLATE AND BOTH RISERS, all three reported from the game and all three the same kind of fault -- a cell laid over a surface whose aspect it was not drawn for. (1) THE RISERS SMEARED. `buildlib.lathe_uv` runs u ONCE around, which is right for a drum and wrong here: this piece is 54.0 units in circumference with a lower riser 0.55 tall, so the port cell ran 923 texels per world unit up the band against 9.4 across it -- anisotropy 98 measured off the built glb, 64.7 on the upper riser -- and the hazard stripes at the foot of that cell pulled out into a flat yellow line round the base. `lathe_uv` takes a `reps` now (it must divide the turn count, so a copy boundary is a real vertex boundary), and each riser wears a BAND of its cell rather than the whole square: the lens row for the lower, the rivet line for the upper, u to 256 px because the port band's own period is 128 px and the bolted panel's is 256, so copies join with nothing to line up by hand. 98 -> 1.7 and 64.7 -> 1.6. The hazard stripes are no longer worn by a riser and that is aspect and not taste: 280 px over 0.55 units cannot be made square. (2) THE DECK READ AS A 3 x 3 PATTERN, which was the ART: cell 0 held three identical panels each way (measured, mean |col - col+171| = 0.27) and `disc_uv` lays a cell once, so the joins landed as a tic-tac-toe at r = +-2.9 and the lid carried them at 40 texels per world unit against the tread's 29 -- two scales of the same grid meeting at the step. Replaced with ONE seamless diamond tile generated for it, level-matched to the sheet at p50 63.7 (the old cell's own) so nothing else on the prop moved, and the underside now takes the whole port cell instead of the riser's narrow band. Still 540 tris, holes 0, coplanar 0. SHEET CELL 0 PROMPT (the sheet lives in the unversioned models-src, so this is its only record): "A SEAMLESS TILING industrial steel tread-plate (diamond-plate) deck surface, seen straight down from above, filling the whole square frame edge to edge. A regular dense grid of small raised diamond treads in staggered rows, roughly 34 diamonds across the image, on dark cool-grey steel. Absolutely NO panel joins, NO seam lines, NO border, NO bolts, NO rivets, NO text, NO vignette, NO centre motif -- one uniform continuous pattern of identical diamonds at one single scale over the entire image, and the pattern must continue across the image edges so the tile repeats invisibly. Very subtle scuffing only, no large stains or highlights." + art/textures.json `style` verbatim, gpt-image-2 at 1024 medium, then resized to the 512 cell and gamma-lifted ^0.876 to land on the old cell's p50 63.7.

wild/tree-conifer-hand.note: hand-modelled off models-src/wild/conifer_build.py, and THE ART IS A GEN PUT THROUGH models-src/wild/sheet_build.py. TWO SHEETS OFF ONE 1k 2x2 GEN, because a 2x2 is four cells and the park needs FIVE: every plant wants a light tone, a DARKER TONE OF THE SAME FOLIAGE and bark, and the conifer's foliage is needles where the broadleaf's and the shrubs' is leaves. The first sheet shipped four, so the conifer's lower two skirts took the dark BROADLEAF cell and the tree wore needles above and leaves below -- reported as its lower half being off the wrong sub-texture, and it was. Splitting is free rather than cheap: tools/models.mjs writes every label its own resized copy, so these glbs already carried a 512 each and sharing one source bought nothing. THE TILING IS IMPOSED AND NOT REQUESTED, because four tiling quadrants in one image is something the model cannot check, and every part of every plant here is a LATHE whose u runs 0..1 once around -- so a cell's LEFT edge column abuts its RIGHT edge column all the way up the seam, which was one hard vertical line down every tree and every shrub. Each cell's INSET band (buildlib.cell insets 2 px, so the columns that meet are 2 and 509 and tiling the full quadrant leaves a 4-px step in the only place it matters) is blended with a copy of itself rolled half a turn, weight 1 at the wrap and smoothstepped to 0 by 40 px: the rolled copy is continuous exactly where the original is not, and the weight is back to zero a few dozen pixels in so the middle of the cell keeps its own contrast. Measured, mean |left-right| against the mean step between neighbouring columns: needle 9.99 -> 9.73 against a grain of 9.65, leaf 12.46 -> 6.96 against 6.52, bark 11.80 -> 7.00 against 7.85, needle-dark 9.99 -> 7.54 against 7.48, leaf-dark 7.18 -> 4.48 against 4.62 -- the wrap is no worse a discontinuity than the art's own grain, and no seam shows in a Blender render at either elevation or 47 degrees of pitch. LEVELS DID NOT MOVE: each cell is multiplied PER CHANNEL IN LINEAR LIGHT onto the mean the crop sheet measured (light 59.8/63.5/57.4, leaf 49.9/53.0/47.7, bark 48.4/47.4/46.7, dark 43.2/45.9/41.2), which is why a vividly green gen ships very nearly neutral -- that IS the park's fitted palette, taken from what the glbs these replace shipped, and holding it is the point. Per channel and not a scalar because the target is a measured triple; the multiply is flat, so nothing clips and the mottle keeps its shape. No baseColor, lift or sat is carried. THE BRIEF IS TWO NUMBERS, and ONE OF THEM HAS SINCE MOVED. FacilityGround.GREEN draws this at h 7.5 and Models.instanced scales by HEIGHT alone, so it is built AT world size and the batch's scale stays 1. scenario-a/spaceship.note: the alien ship of the crash-landing scenario, standing on the hangar's study podium and later on its wilderness pad (render.world.ObjModels). SUPPLIED AS A 584,186-tri master with a 2048 atlas, so this is the decimate route and it takes one cleanly: propstat reads 1 component at 100% and a 1.05x split on the source. tris 100000 and tex 2048 are the SECOND cut and both are the owner's call rather than a fit -- the first shipped 6,000 tris at 1024, which is what texels-per-triangle asks for and which measured 46.1 texels per world unit at h 5.5 against the ground's own 57. At 100k the saucer's ribs and its landing legs are geometry instead of a normal map's suggestion, and the prop is one instance drawn once: it takes the compound from 98k triangles to 276k and holds 60fps on this rig. NO baseColor, and that is the measurement rather than an omission: propstat's 0.52 suggestion is keyed on the 46-52 OUTDOOR family, and this prop's life is spent indoors on a hangar floor, where the repainted interior (floor 95, wall 111) wants ~78. The raw bake lands at 75/72/79, which is that number already. THE EMISSIVE MAP IS A MARKER AND NOT A LIGHT, which is why its strength is 0.35 and not the family's 3: render.world.PropGlow's `lamps` column matches its tints back by normalised hue and gives each family its own colour, beat and phase, so all the map says is WHICH TEXELS belong to which family. IT IS PAINTED PER TEXEL IN THE GAME and the game writes the png: render.PolyPaint (street-debug key T) brushes a world-space capsule resolved through the geometry -- every triangle the sweep reaches has its uv triangle rasterised and each covered texel back-projected barycentrically and tested against the capsule -- and SAVE writes the finished 2048 png through host.debug.writeImage into <userData>/debug/, from where it is copied to models-src/scenario-a/spaceship-emissive.png. tools/models.mjs embeds emissiveSrc VERBATIM, so those bytes are the shipped bytes and the prop on screen after a save is the prop that ships. THE UNIT USED TO BE A TRIANGLE AND THAT IS WHAT THIS REPLACES, for three measured reasons: propstat reads 41 texels/tri at 2048, so at the old 1024 a triangle was about three texels across and every lamp came out a faceted blob; tools/emissive.py's bleed guard kept 1.098% while eating 1.637%, which forced --near, which lit every triangle that merely TOUCHED the selection; and compositing the families with ImageChops.lighter left 893 texels of e0c8e0, a hue 0.73 from amber and 0.62 from cyan against a 0.25 tolerance, matching no family and glowing as nothing. The export now grows each family two texels into the GUTTER ONLY -- texels no triangle covers -- so foreign bleed is zero by construction rather than by a guard that also ate the mask, and nothing painted is ever removed. The 2048 seed was generated once by models-src/scenario-a/spaceship_emissive.py from the last triangle selection (spaceship-paint.json, amber 1795 / cyan 3623 tris) rasterised with no outline and no dilation; that script is not in the loop any more. TWO FAMILIES AND NOT THREE: the near-white crown lens is gone, because white is the hardest marker on this prop (the cap's albedo is bimodal, dark navy shell at luma 66-89 against the glass at 185-250) and two lamps plus a white one read as a light show rather than a machine. Re-seed and re-paint after any change to tris here -- the seed reads the BUILT glb, so the selection follows the decimation, and spaceship-paint.json records the triangle count it was painted against so a stale seed refuses instead of lighting an unrelated surface.

NO baseColor: the bake sampled 67/91/16, luma 75, already inside the INDOOR ~78 band (the 46-52 the tool quotes is the outdoor family), and chroma 75 is the highest in the corp set -- a green that survives a blue lamp is exactly what the accent rule asks for. LIFT 0.83, fitted on the BUILT glb: the bake's own self-occlusion between forty leaves took it to 58.7 srgb, which against a 84-101 carpet is a dark blob rather than a plant. A gamma and not a baseColor, which only multiplies down. The lift STAYS (it is what keeps the forty-leaf self-occlusion off the floor) and a flat linear 0.64 takes the whole thing down with it: 99 -> ~80 srgb by the sRGB transfer, hue untouched because the scalar is flat. propstat's own suggestion of 0.42 is fitted to the OUTDOOR 46-52 family and is a different room.

corp/stairs.note: the corp floor's stairs (objects.Stairs, key stairs), hand-modelled: 2,376 tris, a U-stairwell over FOUR cells -- the stairs cell and the three sealed round it (gen.corp.CorpTemp.stairsCells), whose floor caps render.corp.CorpModel leaves out (FacilityModel.FIT_HOLE). Both flights run from the corridor edge to landings by the window that span both lanes; the next flight down doubles back under the up flight, the next flight up over the down one, cut after 3 steps. The well walls stand on the cell edges, so the wall cells' floor strips stay a ledge round it. Built at WORLD SIZE, origin on the stairs cell centre; its footprint centre and its 6.6 under the floor are put back by CorpStyle.STAIRS_*. Wears stairs-sheet.png (tools/modelsheet.py over the BUILT corp/stairs-tread, -riser, -well and -rail labels), so NO baseColor and NO lift; the tread label's carpet tiles over every tread and landing at one density and its ribbed band is a nosing strip of its own. The well's darkness is COLOR_0 baked by depth (1 at the floor, black at -4.5). buildlib.check: holes 0, coplanar 0, islands 1, texel_off 0. models-src/corp/stairs_build.py.
